review.boundary: The candidate denotes the historical DEC language entry. The original archive is a collection spanning the language, DEC service variants, later ports, listings, and memorabilia. FOCAL-8 has a separate proposed implementation identity.

challenge.method: Checked the exact archive heading, editor and narrator context, timeline and original link against the independently acquired DEC scan cover and printed pp. 1-1–1-2, the separately acquired 1968 manual, and the frozen registry origins.
challenge.results: The archive calls the subject Formula Calculator and gives an interpreter-centered recollection. The linked DEC text expressly identifies both a service program and its conversational command language. Its publisher imprint and documented PDP-8 context establish the language referent. The two historical sources use different expansions of FOCAL and should retain their local wording. The origin occurs once in the frozen candidate ledger.

limitations: Association is limited to the canonical language identity. The archive does not supply equivalence for ports, overlays, or the DEC FOCAL-8 program.
CHM archive details and its linked copy are candidate context, with the 1968 DEC manual bound separately as official documentation for the identity claim.
The linked PDF cover and inspected opening pages identify DEC and the language. That capture’s catalog number and 1968 date come from the archive entry and locator.

proposed_record.name: FOCAL
proposed_record.reason: The archive introduces the historical DEC FOCAL subject and links a DEC technical document that expressly describes its conversational programming language on the PDP-8 family.
